# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-32 (Extended v212)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to winter Year 8. Primary Paris locations: Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, Luxembourg Garden, Rue de Pontoise, Rue Polonceau, Café Corinthe, Rue de l'Étoile, Rue Saint-Louis, Rue du Temple, Rue Vieille-du-Temple, Rue Notre-Dame de Nazareth, Rue Folie-Méricourt, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Petit-Musc, Rue du Normandie, Rue Pont-Aux-Biches, Rue des Marais, Faubourg Saint-Martin, Rue Notre Dame des-Victoires, Faubourg Montmartre, Rue Grange-Batelière, Rue Jacob, Rue de Tournon, Pont au Change, Pont-Neuf, Sewer des Halles, Seine, Sainte-Avoye sewer, Rue Michel-le-Comte, sewer of the Louvre, Montmartre sewer, Rue du Cadran, belt sewer, Saint-Merry, Quay, Passy, Pont de Jéna, Bercy, Amelot sewer, Isle Louviers, Quartier Popincourt, Ménilmontant, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire, Carrefour Boucherat, Corridor Saint-Louis, Saint-Gilles gut, Saint-Sebastian gallery, Arsenal, Faubourg Saint-Honoré, Quartier Saint-Georges, Quartier des Martyrs, gallery des Martyrs, Beautreillis sewer, Quai des Ormes, Grève, Place du Châtelet, Pont Notre-Dame, Quai de la Mégisserie, Boulevard, church of Saint-Paul, Rue du Parc-Royal, Madeleine, Rue Culture-Sainte-Catherine, Blancs-Manteaux, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire, Place Royale, Tuileries. ## English Subplot Summary

**Confirmed rumors**: Fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (confirmed by Wenelle Lindmere to Rovus Prydenridge, winter Year 8).

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford for Dungate. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead for Salcombe; Fenelle followed. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate for Elmhaven (winter Year 6); Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. Gadrek quit milling, took brewery work (autumn Year 7). Kassa Stenson's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Fenelle found Elmhaven work (summer Year 7); Marald followed within month. Zavus Prydenridge apprenticed anew, became ferryman (summer Year 7). Islan Thornmere quit Ostcombe for Dungate (autumn Year 7); Vesmira Thornmere went to Dungate (autumn Year 7). Movie Prydenridge married Luena Stenenridge's only son at Ostcombe; couple lived there. Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest. Havie and Isric Thornmere wed at Ostcombe with half parish present; lived there. Matho Stenson moved from Elmhaven to Staveford (winter Year 7); Fenelle followed Marald to Ravenmere within month. Elra Corrford rode out of Elmhaven; by next market day living in Gulhaven. Red Ismira went along to live in Staveford. Islan Thornmere died of old age at Dungate. Gadrek Prydenridge married Lura Haskick's eldest daughter in chapel at Ostcombe; couple lived there. Luvie Prydenridge and Semor wed at Ostcombe. Luena Stenenridge sent copper chalice by carrier to Yera Stenworth, who received it safely. Yera Haskick swore to Nerine Prydenridge to repair roof of chapel at Kelmere, shook on it. Havie Prydenridge never kept promise to Gadrek (pay old debt); matter abandoned. Luena Stenenridge left Wilwick, settled in Ostcombe. Rozek Stenenridge went along to live in Ostcombe. Luvie Prydenridge gave up weaving, took work as chandler (autumn Year 8). Ismira Stenson gave up being shepherd, took work as scribe (winter Year 8). Gadrek Prydenridge won copper chalice from Yera Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it (winter Year 8). **Tatho Brackick left Salcombe and settled in Wilholt.** **Yewyn Haskick followed him to Wilholt within the month.**

**Solemn promises**: Elra gave Matho promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle promise to plant orchard on slope above Salcombe (summer Year 7). Movie swore to Nerine to plant orchard on slope above Wilholt, shook on it (autumn Year 7).

**New births and marriages (Spring Year 7)**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son Movus Brackick (Wilholt). Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe, had son Istho Stenworth (Ostcombe). Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge had son Febin Prydenridge (Kelmere). Bremira Corrford and Zavus Prydenridge married at Dunstead. Ferald and Zalis Corrley wed at Dunstead (summer Year 7).

**Property transfers**: Kassa Brackick won bone compass from Volan Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it. Kassa Brackick gave amber map to Volan Stenworth (summer Year 8). Kassa Brackick gave bone compass to Ismira (autumn Year 8).

**English characters' current activities (Chapter 32)**: Rovus Prydenridge reads almanac aloud, mispronouncing saints. Wenelle Lindmere argues with carter over oat prices (Salcombe). Pelia Lindmere complains of aching back as usual. Sebin complains of aching back as usual. Rorald Lindmere laughs alone, argues with carter, mends torn sleeve by window, spends evening sorting old letters by candlelight, appears tired. Pelia Lindmere buys ribbon at stall, regrets it. Both remark "price of salt is a scandal."

## Marius and Cosette: Courtship, Revelation, Marriage, and Jean Valjean's Crisis

**Spring Year 6 confessions**: Marius revealed—orphan, lawyer, father colonel and hero. Cosette revealed—raised at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent.

**Barricade and rescue (24 June)**: Éponine revealed leading Marius to barricade, gave letter from Cosette before dying. Marius joined barricade (6 June), witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed. Shot broke collar bone. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished.

**Medical recovery (Chapters 27-30)**: Bullet deflected by pocket-book, serious laceration but not dangerous. Underground journey dislocated collar-bone seriously. Arms slashed with sabre cuts. Head covered with cuts. **7 September (four months after retrieval)**: Doctor declared Marius would recover. When Marius called grandfather "father" three times, Gillenormand agreed to bring Cosette to him.

**Cosette's arrival and revelation (Chapter 31)**: Learned she was not daughter of old man she called father; he was merely kinsman; another Fauchelevent was her real father. She was so full of joy cloud did not last long. She had Marius.

**Cosette's dowry (Chapter 31)**: Five hundred eighty thousand francs constituted legacy by dead person desiring to remain unknown.

**Gillenormand's gifts**: Called Cosette "exquisite darling," "masterpiece," warned half his possessions swallowed in annuity. Overwhelmed her with gallant compliments and presents: robes, lace, parures, ivory bon-bon boxes. Furnished chamber with elegant trifles.

**Wedding ceremony (1 February 1833, church of Saint-Paul)**: **Cosette wore white taffeta petticoat, Binche guipure robe, English point veil, fine pearl necklace, orange flower wreath.** Route: Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. **Two maskers noticed wedding—Spaniard with enormous nose and huge black moustache; young girl masked with loup dressed as gaunt fishwife—held dialogue in low voice.** First coach held Cosette, Aunt Gillenormand, M. Gillenormand, Jean Valjean. Marius came in second coach. Both exchanged vows, signed registers, exchanged rings, knelt side by side under pall of white moire. **During dinner, Basque reported M. Fauchelevent suffering; injured hand paining him; begged excused; would come tomorrow. Had just taken departure.** **Jean Valjean had risen, gained antechamber unperceived during Cosette's command, left during celebration.**

**Jean Valjean's moral crisis (Chapter 31)**: In Cosette's empty bedroom: no sheets on bed. Pillow covered with ticking, without case or lace, laid on blankets. All little feminine objects Cosette attached to carried away; only heavy furniture and four walls remained. Toussaint's bed despoiled. One bed only made up—Jean Valjean's bed. **He opened inseparable portmanteau which never left him.** **Questioned: Should he force himself on this happiness? Should he treat it as belonging to him? Should he remain sort of father, half seen but respected? Should he present himself there as though he had right? Should he bring past to future?** **Remained twelve long hours of winter night, ice-cold, without raising head or uttering word. Motionless as corpse. All at once shuddered convulsively, mouth glued to Cosette's garments, kissed them; then it could be seen he was alive.**

## Javert's Death (Chapter 30)

**Moral transformation**: Javert's certainty crumbled. Duty divided within conscience. Valjean disconcerted him. All axioms crumbled. M. Madeleine reappeared behind Jean Valjean. Benevolent malefactor, merciful, gentle, helpful, clement. Javert constrained to admit monster existed. Supreme anguish was loss of certainty. Code no longer anything but stump. **Suicide (evening, Place du Châtelet)**: Took off hat, placed it on edge of quay. Tall black figure appeared erect on parapet, bent over towards Seine, drew self up, fell straight down into shadows; dull splash followed. Javert drowned.

## Marius's Crisis of Conscience (Chapter 32)

**Jean Valjean's revelation (morning after wedding—17 February)**: Jean Valjean appeared very pale, eyes hollow and sunken by sleeplessness. Black coat bore weary folds. **Proclaimed: "I am an ex-convict."** Proceeding from mouth of M. Fauchelevent and entering ear of Marius overshot possible. Marius stood with mouth wide open.

**Jean Valjean's justification**: "I am an honest man. I should not be so if, through my fault, you had continued to esteem me; now that you despise me, I am so. I have that fatality hanging over me that, not being able to ever have anything but stolen consideration, that consideration humiliates me. In order that I may respect myself, it is necessary that I should be despised. Then I straighten up again. I am a galley-slave who obeys his conscience." Declared conscience implacable; duty places one in hell where one feels God beside you. Stated he had entered into engagements with himself; keeps them. Declared he revealed situation himself—nothing forced him. If police arrived, he would be exposed through his own act, not another's. Chose danger over security of false name.

**Marius's shock and self-recrimination**: Inward shudder of hideous enlightenment flashed through Marius; idea made him quiver. Addressed Jean Valjean almost like angry person: "But why do you tell me all this? Who forces you? You could have kept secret. What is your motive?" After Jean Valjean's departure, Marius pleaded with him not to tell Cosette: "She does not know what it is, it would terrify her. What, a convict!" Jean Valjean dropped into armchair, hid face in hands, seized with convulsion, threw himself against back of chair as though to gain breath, letting arms fall. Face inundated with tears.

**Marius's reflective reckoning (post-wedding)**: Marius questioned whether he had failed in divination, prudence, or wits regarding Jean Valjean's true nature. Admitted chimerical and visionary side of his nature—internal cloud peculiar to many organizations, which in paroxysms of passion and sorrow dilates and invades entire man, rendering him nothing more than conscience bathed in mist. Recalled that during six or seven ecstatic weeks in Rue Plumet, he had not even spoken to Cosette of Gorbeau hovel drama, nor mentioned Thénardiers, nor named them even when he encountered Éponine. Accounted for this: benumbed state, intoxication with Cosette, love absorbing everything, vague dull instinct impelling him to conceal and abolish that redoubtable adventure in his memory—contact he dreaded, in which he did not wish to play part.

**Marius's reconciliation with Jean Valjean's revelation**: Weighed everything: even had he discovered Jean Valjean was convict, it would not have changed him or Cosette. He would not have drawn back. Would have adored her no less. Would not have refrained from marrying her. Therefore: nothing to regret, nothing to reproach himself. All was well. Love had bandaged his eyes to lead him to paradise.

**Jean Valjean's moral grandeur**: Moreover, Jean Valjean had himself revealed situation. Nothing forced him. If anyone learned who he was, through himself. In avowal there was something more than acceptance of humiliation: acceptance of peril. For condemned man, mask is not mask but shelter; false name is security. He had rejected false name. Galley-slave might have hidden forever in honest family; had withstood temptation. Through conscientious scruple. Explained with irresistible accents of truth. Whatever Jean Valjean might be, undoubtedly conscience awakening. Mysterious rehabilitation begun; scruples controlled him long. Fits of justice and goodness not characteristic of vulgar natures. Awakening of conscience is grandeur of soul.

**Marius's new doubt—Javert and vengeance**: Marius recalled distinctly that recollection reappeared in emotions like sympathetic ink at application of heat. Jean Valjean had been in barricade. Had not fought there. What came for? Spectre rose and replied: "Javert." Recalled funereal sight of Jean Valjean dragging pinioned Javert out of barricade. Still heard behind corner of little Rue Mondétour that frightful pistol shot. Obviously hatred between police spy and galley-slave. One in other's way. Jean Valjean had gone to barricade purpose of revenging himself. Arrived late. Probably knew Javert prisoner there. Corsican vendetta penetrated certain lower strata, became law there. Criminal in path of repentance may be scrupulous in theft, unscrupulous in vengeance. **Jean Valjean had killed Javert. At least, seemed evident.**

**Marius's metaphysical anguish**: What melancholy sport of Providence placed that child in contact with that man? Are chains for two forged on high? God take pleasure in coupling angel with demon? Crime and innocence room-mates in mysterious galleys of wretchedness? In defiling of condemned persons called human destiny, can two brows pass side by side—one ingenuous, one formidable, one bathed in divine whiteness of dawn, one forever blemished by flash of eternal lightning? Who arranged inexplicable pairing? In what manner, consequence of what prodigy, had community of life been established between celestial little creature and old criminal? Wolf loved lamb. Fierce creature adored feeble one. During space of nine years, angel had monster as her point of support. Cosette's childhood and girlhood, advent in daylight, virginal growth towards life and light, sheltered by hideous devotion. Questions exfoliated into innumerable enigmas. Abysses yawned at bottoms of abysses. Marius could no longer bend over Jean Valjean without becoming dizzy. **What was this man-precipice?**
